1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 6-11) (c. 200 BC)

Where the Hebrew Bible's 'sons of God' (b'nei ha'elohim) saw the daughters of men, the Ethiopian Tewahedo tradition reads through 1 Enoch's expansion: the Watchers, two hundred angels under Semjâzâ, descend on Mount Hermon and bind themselves by oath to take human wives. The corruption is not human alone but angelic-human, requiring the Flood as a cosmic — not merely punitive — purgation. The Tewahedo canon is the only Christian canon to receive 1 Enoch as Scripture, making this reading load-bearing for its theology of evil.
